[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
Robert Glasgow was baptised on 28 May 1665 at St Cuthbert's, Edinburgh, son of [[Glasgow-3337|James Glasgow]] and [[Glessie-1|Annapill Glessie]]. The baptism is indexed by FamilySearch.<ref name="baptism">FamilySearch, “Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:F316-F84 Robert Glasgow, 1665]. The indexed 28 May date is treated as baptism, not a proved birth date.</ref>

A Robert Glasgow was in Alexander Ainslie's service in North Leith in 1694. On 16 July he gave a receipt in Ainslie's name for bottles supplied to the Earl of Breadalbane; on 3 October the poll tax placed Robert among four servants in Ainslie's household. The same employer, business and short interval make those two adult records an exceptionally strong one-person identification.<ref name="receipt">National Records of Scotland, Breadalbane Muniments, GD112/15/59, item 24, Robert Glasgow receipt in Alexander Ainslie's name, 16 July 1694; [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/details.aspx?reference=GD112%2F15%2F59 catalogue].</ref><ref name="poll">National Records of Scotland, Scottish Exchequer poll tax, North Leith, E70/4/10, image 11, 3 October 1694; original image via Scotland's People Virtual Volumes.</ref>

The baptised child and the adult servant are combined here as the best current identification: a man baptised in the Edinburgh area in 1665 would have been about 29 in North Leith in 1694. Neither adult record names his parents, so this cross-record identification remains inferred. No spouse or children are established. Robert's birth place is not independently recorded. The 1694 records do not call him a glassmaker, though he handled a bottle transaction.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-3077]] is assessed at 98% (proved). Robert's 28 May 1665 St Cuthbert's index names James Glasgow and Annapill Glasse. The full James/Annapill couple and St Cuthbert’s sequence identify the selected record father.

Confident for the recorded 1665 child; James’s earlier ancestry and Clerk-household identification remain separate.

Next useful test: Use the original entry if a competing Robert or parental couple is proposed.

Source basis already held: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:F316-F84 FamilySearch, “Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” Robert Glasgow, 1665 (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:F316-F84). The indexed 28 May date is treated as baptism, not a proved birth date.]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


The former adult profile [[Glasgow-4149]] estimated birth about 1670 and North Leith as birth place from his adult service. Those were uncertain estimates rather than birth evidence. The 1665 baptism now supplies the structured early date, while the Leith service remains in the biography. Other same-name baptism candidates, including [[Glasgow-3011|Robert baptised at Glencorse in 1676]], were considered. The 1665 St Cuthbert's baptism has the closer Edinburgh-area locality and better age fit; the original register and any Ainslie papers could strengthen or overturn this inference.

A modern glass-industry history calls the servant a glassmaker and dates the poll-tax appearance to 1695. The original record is dated 3 October 1694 and calls him a servant; the occupational claim remains unproved.<ref name="turnbull">Jill Turnbull, [https://era.ed.ac.uk/server/api/core/bitstreams/fe29343e-a341-412e-85bd-96afca6214e5/content “The Scottish Glass Industry, 1610–1750”] (PhD thesis, University of Edinburgh, 1999), pp. 171, 202, 324, 350.</ref>
